name: PageRank
description: PageRank is a link analysis algorithm that assigns a numerical weighting to each element of a hyperlinked set of documents, such as the World Wide Web, with the purpose of measuring its relative importance within the set. It was the foundation of Google's original search engine ranking system.
how_it_works: PageRank treats the web as a directed graph where pages are nodes and links are edges. It models a 'random surfer' who clicks links randomly. The algorithm iteratively computes scores: each page distributes its current PageRank equally among its outgoing links, and each page's new rank is the sum of incoming ranks. The process converges to a stationary distribution representing page importance.

complexity.time: O(k * n) where k is iterations and n is number of pages
complexity.space: O(n) for storing the graph and ranks

key_parameters: damping_factor (typically 0.85): probability of continuing to click links vs jumping randomly
max_iterations: maximum number of iterations to prevent infinite loops
teleportation_probability: probability of random jump to any page
pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Initialize all pages with rank = 1/n. Repeat until convergence: for each page p: new_rank[p] = (1-d)/n + d * sum(rank[q]/out_degree[q] for all q linking to p). Then normalize ranks so they sum to 1. The damping factor d (usually 0.85) represents the probability of following a link vs. teleporting randomly.
